Proposed alternative to slide 8, preserving the original. The €53k detection-chain allocation is user-provided and covers CZT detector, front-end electronics and waveform DAQ. Supplier quotations previously inspected total €29,280 plus €21,990.50 including VAT; reconcile rounded project allocations on the budget slide. The graph calculates total interaction probability 1-exp(-mu*rho*t) with xraylib total attenuation coefficients, normal incidence, bulk densities Si 2.33, Ge 5.32 and Cd0.9Zn0.1Te 5.8 g/cm3, thicknesses 450 µm, 1 mm and 2 mm. It is not a measured photopeak-efficiency result and excludes windows, dead layers, escape and charge-collection losses. At 22.2 keV the model gives approximately 29.3% for Si and 100% for CZT. Channel calibration, charge-sharing reconstruction and pile-up analysis are planned PRISM development activities. The scientific motivation is efficient detection of weak fluorescence and a calibrated room-temperature spectroscopic readout, with performance qualification on the following slide.

Alternative to slide 9: why PRISM develops a custom multichannel CZT detection chain. The custom scope is a specified 20-pixel linear sensor, dedicated low-noise front-end channels, accessible waveforms and detector-specific calibration/reconstruction. These design choices allow response and counting losses to be characterized under fluorescence-XAS operating conditions. Segmentation distributes count rate but does not by itself increase solid angle; no quantitative collection-area gain is asserted here. This slide does not claim commercial alternatives cannot provide any of these capabilities, or that the exact 20-channel count has already been proven optimal. Sources: FINAL/Progetto.pdf detector baseline, WP2 and MS2, and QUOTAZIONI/Quotazione_CZT.pdf. The plotted pulse-selection result is prior CZT experience, not a qualification of the planned PRISM detector. No illustrative detector image is presented as a design drawing. M15 targets apply under selected XAS operating conditions: energy resolution ≤2% at Ag Kα 22.2 keV, dead time <10%, pile-up contamination <5%; intrinsic efficiency target >90% at 50 keV remains in the proposal. The experimental proof of pulse-shape methods motivates waveform access; application to the custom detector is project work.

PRISM assigns 1.7 FTE at INFN-LNF to delivery: Simone Manti 1.0, Alessandro Scordo 0.3, Massimiliano Bazzi 0.3, Catalina Curceanu 0.1. The table maps responsibilities to the work packages.

The existing VOXES equipment and laboratory infrastructure provide the experimental foundation. The established University of Palermo collaboration and SIDDHARTA/KAONNIS experience contribute to CZT geometry, front-end electronics, calibration and reconstruction. VIP shares the challenges of weak hard-X-ray signals and pulse-shape analysis.

ENRICH WG3 (Software Advancement) connects ray tracing with other Monte Carlo tools and integrated-model validation. Manti is co-leader; Manuel Sánchez del Río is WG leader and principal developer of SHADOW4. Direct interaction supports the crystal-optics modelling and SHADOW4–GEANT4 workflow in WP1. The existing photograph shows Manti with Sánchez del Río. This support does not by itself validate PRISM's predictions; benchmark measurements and analytical comparisons remain necessary.

Due2Lab's signed letter expresses support for PRISM and interest in possible future technical exchanges on CZT sensor architectures, detector characterization and application requirements. Specific contributions would be agreed separately. This is documented industrial interest, not a guarantee of delivery, funding or an already contracted development activity.

Further synergies: SPHINX for precision angular scanning and alignment; EuAPS and AQUA for complementary XAS methods and preparation of future experiments after laboratory validation. Rigaku and Quantum Design have also provided letters of support.
